author: @jeremyfowers

evidence.api_compatibility: No breaking changes. No code was modified, so no existing command, flag, config value, API call, saved file, or documented behavior stops working on upgrade.
evidence.documentation: The new spec at docs/dev/specs/container-backends.md is comprehensive (462 lines) and well-structured: design philosophy, scope, class architecture with Mermaid diagram, command contract with tables, setup by install type for both user-started and system-service scenarios, image update workflow, and detailed appendices comparing against Ramalama and AI Cockpit. mkdocs.yml was updated to group spec pages under a Specs nav section, including the new container-backends.md and the existing spec-writing-guide.md. The PR was labeled documentation, consistent with the change type.
evidence.manual_release_testing: This commit is documentation-only. It adds a design spec for container backends — a future feature — and updates mkdocs navigation. No shipped code, no API change, no CLI flag, no new config. The spec itself is not user-reachable behavior. No manual release testing is required.
evidence.post_approval_commits: Three commits were added after @superm1's first approval: (1) docs: allocate the lemonade sub-UID range in the install scripts, past existing ranges — moved subordinate ID allocation from ExecStartPre in the unit file to install scripts, with idempotent behavior. (2) docs: mount a model directory one file at a time, resolved through symlinks — refined the model mount table to clarify per-file mounting through symlinks. (3) docs: relax lemond-user.service for rootless Podman, and keep the system unit's other protections — clarified that systemd applies mount-based protections before switching accounts, so LockPersonality/RestrictRealtime remain effective. All three are documentation-only refinements that stay within the approved scope and do not change behavior, security, or API. They were also within the spirit of the review, addressing earlier inline comments.
evidence.review: PR #3697 received two approval reviews: @superm1 approved at 2026-10-06T13:38:17Z and @Geramy approved at 2026-10-06T18:05:19Z. @superm1 has containers, Docker, and security listed as a subject-matter area in docs/dev/contribute.md, meeting the expertise bar. The spec went through substantive inline discussion with @abn on SELinux labeling, ContainerPolicy field naming (repository→image), and memlock_unlimited removal, and with @Geramy on ipc_host removal. All discussion points were addressed before approval. No release-blocking corner cases were missed — the spec is intentionally scoped to fundamentals and defers broader Linux support to future PRs.
evidence.security: No security concerns. This is a pure documentation change. The spec itself discusses security hardening (cap-drop=all, no-new-privileges, seccomp defaults, SELinux) for future implementation but does not introduce or modify any security-sensitive code.
evidence.tests: The PR changes only two files: docs/dev/specs/container-backends.md (new, 462 lines) and mkdocs.yml (+4/-1). No code was changed, so no code tests are affected. No tests were weakened or deleted. The spec references CI validation patterns (validate_llamacpp.yml, validate_containers.yml) for future implementation.

subject: docs: add the container backends spec (#3697)
summary: Adds a 462-line spec document at docs/dev/specs/container-backends.md that defines how Lemonade will support Linux container backends (Podman and Docker) for single-GPU inference, including class architecture, run-command contracts, setup-by-install-type procedures, and detailed comparison with Ramalama and AI Cockpit conventions.
verdict_reason: This is a documentation-only PR to a design spec, approved by two reviewers including a containers subject-matter expert, with no code changes, no breaking API, and no security impact.
